paragraphs: Nora arrived at the community garden early on Saturday to prepare for its first open day. At 8:15, the front gate was still locked. She called the caretaker and asked, “{{mask_1}}?” {{red:Leo was usually at the gate by eight}}, but his phone went straight to voicemail. Nora checked the blue cabinet for the spare key. “{{mask_2}}” she asked her neighbor, Sam, who had helped organize the event.

They found the key, opened the gate, and went to fill the watering cans. The tank gauge was nearly empty, even though the volunteers had filled it the night before. “{{mask_3}}” Nora wondered aloud. Sam spotted a small leak near the valve. A message about the open day was still sitting in the group chat as a draft, so Nora turned to Sam. “{{mask_4}}” He apologized and sent it to the neighborhood list. Nearby, the seedlings had grown strong enough to leave their trays. “{{mask_5}}” Nora asked, and Sam agreed they could transplant them before visitors arrived.

Rain was still tapping on the greenhouse roof, although the forecast had said it would clear by nine. “{{mask_6}}” Nora asked as she looked at the gray sky. The covered patio was dry and available, so Sam suggested moving the welcome table there. “{{mask_7}}” he said. Their delivery of compost was scheduled to arrive before noon, and the driver had confirmed the time that morning. Nora glanced at her watch. “{{mask_8}}” she asked. Before they began planting, Sam picked up a tray without a label. “{{mask_9}}” Nora reminded him. Maya had promised to bring the labels from the garden shed. “{{mask_10}}” Sam asked, looking toward the path.

While they waited, Nora noticed that the mint and basil were growing in deep shade. “{{mask_11}}” she asked. Sam moved the pots to a sunnier spot. Then they turned the new sign around: its message had been facing the garden wall instead of the road. “{{mask_12}}” Nora said. Omar, a new volunteer, arrived with a box of gloves. Sam had met him at the planning meeting on Tuesday, but Nora had missed it. “{{mask_13}}” Sam asked as he introduced them. The workshop was listed for ten o’clock, and it was already ten past. “{{mask_14}}” Nora said, checking the printed schedule.

A heavier shower swept across the garden, so the team carried their supplies under the covered patio. “{{mask_15}}” Maya asked, pointing to the open meeting room next door. They moved the seed trays inside. The weather app still showed rain, despite an earlier prediction of a clear morning. “{{mask_16}}” Omar asked. Sam checked the safety notice beside the entrance. It instructed the organizers to keep the side door unlocked during public events. “{{mask_17}}” Nora asked, and Omar went to check it. Ben had spent the morning repairing the leaking hose, but water was still dripping from the valve. “{{mask_18}}” Maya asked when she saw him set down his tools.

By late morning, the rain had eased and the first visitors were arriving. The volunteers had prepared a short walk through the vegetable beds. “{{mask_19}}” Nora asked as a family paused at the entrance. Sam offered to lead the tour. Children crowded around the herb pots, and neighbors began asking questions about the compost. Nora looked across the busy garden and smiled. “{{mask_20}}” she asked Sam. He nodded; even with the unexpected rain and repairs, the open day had turned into a success.
